title: Water Conservation
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Science and Technology; not yet checked by a CBC Science and Technology teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Start with a real measure: how many cups of water run away while a tap is left on for one minute (collect it in a basin and measure). Rainwater harvesting from the school roof is the second anchor.

skills.key_step: The child says water conservation means using water carefully and keeping it from being wasted or polluted, so there is enough now and later.

floor.prerequisite: Knows ways water is stored at home.
floor.question: Name one container used to store water at home.
floor.answer: for example a jerrycan or a tank

representations: a basin under a running tap for one minute
a picture of a full and an empty water tank
a word map: save, reuse, keep clean
steps: Run a tap into a basin for one minute and measure the water.
Ask how much was needed to wash hands.
Conserving: use only what is needed, reuse, keep it clean, all year.

board.do: Draw a tank with a tap dripping.

board.say: How much water does this waste in a day?

board.do: Write "conserve = use carefully, waste none, keep clean".

listen_for: store it and never use it
misconceptions.ask: If we never use the tank water, what was it for?
misconceptions.repair: Conserving means using water carefully, not never using it.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to rivers in a long drought?
misconceptions.repair: Rain does not always come; water can run short.

misconceptions.ask: Does a running tap waste water even if it is clean?
misconceptions.repair: Conserving covers saving water as well as keeping it clean.

misconceptions.ask: Where does dry-season water come from?
misconceptions.repair: Save water all year so there is enough in the dry season.

checks.question: What does it mean to conserve water?
checks.answer: to use water carefully and not waste or pollute it

checks.question: Should a school save water in the rainy season? Why?
checks.answer: Yes, so stored water lasts into the dry season

skills.key_step: The child names ways to save water at home and school (turn off taps, fix leaks, collect rainwater, reuse water safely, use a basin not a running tap) and picks the saving way in a story.

floor.question: Is leaving a tap running a way to save water?

representations: a leaking tap and a bucket under it
a chart of methods at home and at school
steps: Close taps when soaping hands or brushing teeth.
Reuse water for plants and floors, never for drinking.
contexts: a rainy afternoon with a roof gutter

board.do: Draw a roof with a gutter and an empty tank.
Ask what happens to the tank when it rains.
Wait for the child to say it fills.
Ask the child to draw one more way to save water at school.

listen_for: leave it running, it is quicker
misconceptions.ask: How many cups ran away in one minute?
misconceptions.repair: Close the tap while you soap or brush.

misconceptions.ask: Which uses less water: a hose or a watering can?
misconceptions.repair: A watering can or a basin uses less water than a running hose or tap.

misconceptions.ask: What can we put under the gutter?
misconceptions.repair: Rainwater can be collected and used.
Used water is for plants and floors, not drinking or cooking.

checks.question: Give one way to save water when brushing teeth.
checks.answer: turn off the tap or use a cup of water

checks.question: What is a safe use for water left after washing vegetables?

skills.key_step: The child gives reasons to conserve water that reach beyond the family: water is limited, people, animals and plants need it, saving it means there is enough in the dry season and for others.

floor.question: Name one way to save water at school.
floor.answer: close taps, harvest rainwater or fix leaks

representations: a map from the river to the tap
pictures of animals and crops in a drought
steps: Trace where tap water comes from.
List who needs it: people, animals, crops.
Say what happens when it runs low.
Give the reason: saving water keeps enough for all.
contexts: a borehole shared by a village

board.do: Draw a river, a pipe and a tap.

board.say: What happens to the tap if the river runs low?

board.do: Write people, animals and plants under the river.

misconceptions.ask: Would we still save water if it were free?
misconceptions.repair: Saving money is one reason; there is a limited amount for everyone.

misconceptions.ask: What do cows and crops drink?
misconceptions.repair: Animals and plants need water too.

misconceptions.ask: Do the rains always come on time?
misconceptions.repair: Rains can fail; saved water carries us through.

misconceptions.ask: Where does the pipe get its water?
misconceptions.repair: Taps bring water from rivers, dams and boreholes that can run low.

checks.question: Give one reason why water should be conserved.
checks.answer: it is limited; people, animals and plants need it; so it lasts the dry season

checks.question: Where does tap water come from?
checks.answer: a river, dam, borehole or tank
